Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run, slide and swing. They saw many things: trees, flowers, birds and dogs. But they also saw something unusual. It was big and round and shiny. It was in the sky, but not very high.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it is a balloon."

They ran to the big thing. They wanted to touch it. But when they got closer, they heard a noise. It was like a beep. And then a door opened. Out came a little green man. He had two eyes, a nose, a mouth and ears. But he also had a long tail and four arms.

"Hello," the green man said. "I am Zog. I come from another planet. Do you want to be my friends?"

Lily and Ben were scared. They did not know what to say. They looked at each other. Then they looked at Zog. He smiled. He did not look mean. He looked friendly.

"Hi," Lily said. "I am Lily. This is Ben. We are from Earth. We want to be your friends."

Zog was happy. He clapped his four hands. He said, "Yay! I have new friends. Do you want to see my spaceship?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They were curious. They followed Zog into the big thing. They saw many buttons, lights and screens. Zog showed them how to fly the spaceship. They had fun. They flew around the park. They waved to the other children. They saw the sun, the moon and the stars.

They had an unusual adventure. They learned new things. They made a new friend. They said, "Thank you, Zog. You are very nice. We hope to see you again."

Zog said, "You are welcome, Lily and Ben. You are very nice too. I hope to see you again. Goodbye."

He landed the spaceship. He gave them a hug. He went back inside. The door closed. The spaceship beeped. It flew away. It disappeared in the sky.

Lily and Ben ran back to their parents. They told them what they saw. Their parents did not believe them. They thought they made up a story. But Lily and Ben knew it was true. They smiled. They had a secret. They had a special friend. They had a wonderful day.

Timmy liked to spin. He spun in his room, he spun in the yard, he spun in the park. He spun so fast that he felt dizzy and happy. He liked to spin with his toys, too. He had a big ball, a small car, a soft bear, and a shiny bottle. He spun them all on the floor and watched them go round and round.

One day, he found a new toy in the kitchen. It was a chubby can with a label that had a picture of a tomato. He thought it looked like a ball, so he took it to his room and spun it on the floor. It spun very fast and made a loud noise. Timmy laughed and clapped his hands.

But then, something bad happened. The can hit the wall and broke open. Red juice and seeds came out and splashed everywhere. Timmy's room was a mess. He was scared and sad. He heard his mom coming and knew he was in trouble.

"Timmy, what did you do?" his mom asked, seeing the red stains on the carpet, the bed, and the walls. She was angry and worried.

"I'm sorry, mom. I was spinning the can. I thought it was a ball. I didn't know it had juice inside," Timmy said, crying.

Mom sighed and hugged him. She was not happy, but she understood. She knew Timmy liked to spin, but he had to learn to be careful.

"Timmy, you can't spin everything. Some things are not toys. Some things can break and make a mess. You have to look at the label and see what's inside. Do you understand?" she said.

Timmy nodded and wiped his tears. He said he was sorry again and helped mom clean the room. He learned his lesson. He still liked to spin, but he only spun his toys. He never spun a can again.

One day, a child named Tom wanted to play with his toy car. He loved his toy car very much. It was red and shiny and fast. He took it outside and drove it on the sidewalk. He made loud noises with his mouth. Vroom, vroom!

But then, he saw another child with a bigger toy car. It was blue and shiny and faster. The other child drove it on the street. He made louder noises with his mouth. Vroom, vroom, vroom!

Tom felt sad. He wanted the bigger toy car. He thought it was better than his toy car. He thought the other child was lucky. He thought he was not.

He walked up to the other child and said, "Can I play with your toy car? Please?"

The other child looked at Tom and said, "No, you can't. This is my toy car. Go away!"

Tom felt angry. He wanted the bigger toy car. He thought it was not fair. He thought the other child was mean. He thought he was tough.

He pushed the other child and grabbed his toy car. He ran away with it. He made loud noises with his mouth. Vroom, vroom, vroom!

But then, he heard a louder noise behind him. It was a big car. It was real and shiny and faster. It honked its horn. Honk, honk!

Tom was scared. He dropped the bigger toy car and ran to the sidewalk. He saw the other child crying and holding his toy car. He felt sorry. He wanted to say sorry. He thought he was wrong.

He walked up to the other child and said, "I'm sorry. I was bad. Can we be friends?"

The other child looked at Tom and said, "It's okay. I'm sorry too. I was mean. Yes, we can be friends."

They smiled at each other and hugged. They played with their toy cars together. They made loud noises with their mouths. Vroom, vroom, vroom!

They were happy. They thought they were lucky. They thought they were good. They thought they were tough.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play games. Today they play a game with cards. Lily has a large card with a red heart. Tom has a small card with a black spade.

"Who will win?" Lily asks.

"I will win," Tom says. "My card is black. Black is better than red."

"No, I will win," Lily says. "My card is large. Large is better than small."

They show their cards to Mom. Mom smiles.

"Both of you are winners," Mom says. "You played well and had fun. That is what matters. And you both have love in your hearts. Love is better than any card."

Lily and Tom hug Mom. They are happy. They love Mom and they love each other. They put away their cards and play another game.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their toys. They saw an old man sitting on a bench. He had a long beard and a hat. He was holding a book.

"Who is he?" Lily asked Ben.

"I don't know. Maybe he is a wizard," Ben said.

They walked closer to the old man. He smiled at them and said hello.

"Hello, sir. What are you reading?" Lily asked.

"I'm reading a story about a brave and honest knight who saved a princess from a dragon," the old man said.

"Wow, that sounds exciting. Can you tell us the story?" Ben asked.

"Sure, I can. Come and sit with me," the old man said.

He pointed to a picture in the book. It showed the knight riding a horse and holding a sword.

"This is the knight. His name is Arthur. He was very brave and honest. He always helped people who were in trouble," the old man said.

He pointed to another picture. It showed the princess in a tower and the dragon breathing fire.

"This is the princess. Her name is Gwen. She was very kind and beautiful. She was trapped in the tower by the dragon. The dragon was very mean and greedy. He wanted to keep her for himself," the old man said.

He pointed to the last picture. It showed the knight fighting the dragon and the princess cheering.

"This is the end of the story. Arthur fought the dragon and wounded him with his sword. The dragon ran away and never came back. Arthur freed Gwen from the tower and they hugged each other. They were very happy and grateful. They became friends and lived happily ever after," the old man said.

Lily and Ben clapped their hands and cheered.

"That was a great story. Thank you, sir," Lily said.

"Yes, thank you. You are very nice and smart," Ben said.

The old man smiled and said, "You're welcome, children. You are very polite and curious. I'm glad you liked the story. It's one of my favorites."

They talked for a while and then said goodbye. Lily and Ben went back to their toys and pretended to be knights and princesses. They had a lot of fun. The old man watched them and smiled. He was happy too.

Tom and Ben were friends who liked to play music. Tom had a trumpet that he got from his dad. Ben had a drum that he made from a can and a stick. They would play songs together and have fun.

One day, Tom saw a new trumpet in a shop window. It was shiny and big and had many buttons. Tom wanted the new trumpet very much. He was envious of anyone who had a better trumpet than him. He thought his old trumpet was not good enough.

He asked his dad to buy him the new trumpet, but his dad said no. He said that Tom should be happy with what he had and take good care of it. He said that the new trumpet was too expensive and that Tom was not ready for it.

Tom was angry and sad. He did not listen to his dad. He hid his old trumpet under his bed and did not play it anymore. He hoped that his dad would change his mind and get him the new trumpet.

But his dad did not change his mind. And Tom's old trumpet did not get any love. It got dusty and dirty and rusty. It started to rot. The sound became bad and the buttons got stuck.

One day, Ben came to visit Tom. He wanted to play music with him. He brought his drum and asked Tom to get his trumpet. Tom felt ashamed and did not want to show his trumpet to Ben. He said that he did not want to play music anymore.

Ben was surprised and sad. He liked to play music with Tom. He asked him why he did not want to play music anymore. Tom did not answer. He just looked away.

Ben looked under Tom's bed and saw the trumpet. He pulled it out and saw how rotten it was. He was shocked and sad. He asked Tom what happened to his trumpet. Tom did not answer. He just cried.

Ben felt sorry for Tom. He said that he liked Tom's trumpet and that it was a good trumpet. He said that he did not care about the new trumpet in the shop window. He said that he cared about Tom and their friendship.

He said that Tom should not be envious of others and that he should be grateful for what he had. He said that Tom should take good care of his trumpet and his friends. He said that Tom should play music with him again and have fun.

Tom realized that Ben was right. He felt sorry for being envious and for neglecting his trumpet and his friend. He hugged Ben and said that he was sorry. He said that he liked his trumpet and that it was a good trumpet. He said that he liked Ben and that he was a good friend.

He said that he wanted to play music with Ben again and have fun. He asked Ben to help him clean his trumpet and make it sound good again. Ben agreed and smiled. They cleaned the trumpet and played songs together and had fun.

The moral of the story is: Be happy with what you have and take good care of it. Do not be envious of others and lose what you have. Cherish your friends and play music with them.

Sam had a big bag of marbles. He liked to play with them and make them roll and shine. He had many colors and shapes of marbles. Some were big and some were small. Some were smooth and some were bumpy.

One day, he went to the park with his mom. He saw a boy who had a very special marble. It was red and blue and had a star inside. Sam thought it was the most powerful marble he had ever seen. He wanted to have it.

"Hi, I'm Sam. What's your name?" he asked the boy.

"I'm Max. Do you like my marble?" the boy said.

"Yes, it's very pretty and powerful. Can I see it?" Sam said.

"Sure, but be careful. It's my favorite marble," Max said. He gave the marble to Sam.

Sam held the marble in his hand. He felt its weight and warmth. He looked at the star and wondered how it got there. He wished he could keep it.

"Can I have your marble?" he asked Max.

"No, you can't. It's mine. Give it back," Max said.

"Please, I'll give you anything. I have many marbles in my bag. You can choose any one you want," Sam said.

"No, I don't want your marbles. I only want my marble. It's the best marble in the world. It's my lucky marble. It makes me happy," Max said.

Sam felt sad. He wanted to make Max happy, but he also wanted the powerful marble. He didn't know what to do. He looked at his mom. She smiled and said:

"Sam, you have to give back the marble to Max. It's his marble, not yours. You can't take something that belongs to someone else. You have to respect his choice. Maybe you can be friends and play together with your marbles. Sharing is more fun than spending."

Sam nodded. He gave back the marble to Max. He said:

"I'm sorry, Max. I didn't mean to be rude. Your marble is very nice, but you can keep it. I have many marbles too. Do you want to play with me?"

Max smiled. He said:

"Thank you, Sam. You are very kind. I'm sorry I was angry. Your marbles are very nice too. Yes, I want to play with you."

Sam and Max became friends. They played with their marbles and had fun. They learned to share and respect each other. They both felt happy.

Sara and Tom were friends who liked to play with toys. They had many toys, but they also liked to look at the screen. The screen showed them funny pictures and sounds. Sometimes they laughed and clapped at the screen.

One day, Sara and Tom found a new toy in the toy box. It was a small screen that had buttons and lights. They were curious and wanted to play with it. They took turns to press the buttons and see what happened. The screen made noises and changed colors. They were happy and excited.

But then, Sara and Tom started to argue. Sara wanted to keep the screen for herself. She said, "This is my screen. I found it first. You can't have it." Tom was angry and said, "No, this is our screen. We share it. You are not nice." They pulled and pushed the screen, trying to take it from each other.

The screen did not like this. It did not belong to Sara or Tom. It belonged to someone else. It was a gift from a kind aunt who wanted to surprise them. The screen was sad and scared. It did not want to be broken or lost. It wanted to be loved and cared for.

The screen made a loud beep and flashed a message. It said, "Please stop fighting. I am not your toy. I am a gift. Please give me back to the toy box. Thank you." Sara and Tom were surprised and ashamed. They realized they were wrong. They said sorry to each other and to the screen. They put the screen back in the toy box and hugged. They decided to play with their other toys and be cheerful and kind.

The moral of the story is: Do not fight over things that do not belong to you. Be respectful and grateful for what you have. Share and play nicely with your friends.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play games together. One day, they play a game with cards. The cards have numbers and pictures on them. Sara and Ben take turns to pick a card and show it to each other. They have to say the number and the picture out loud. If they say it right, they get a point. If they say it wrong, they lose a point. The one with the most points at the end wins.

Sara is good at the game. She knows all the numbers and pictures. She picks a card and says, "Four, dog." She gets a point. She picks another card and says, "Six, fish." She gets another point. She picks a third card and says, "Eight, cake." She gets another point. She has three points. She is happy.

Ben is not so good at the game. He does not know all the numbers and pictures. He picks a card and says, "Three, cat." He is wrong. The card has a three and a hat. He loses a point. He picks another card and says, "Five, bird." He is wrong again. The card has a five and a hand. He loses another point. He picks a third card and says, "Seven, car." He is right. He gets a point. He has minus one point. He is sad.

Sara sees that Ben is sad. She wants to make him happy. She has an idea. She says, "Ben, do you want to mail these cards to grandma? She will like them. She will write us a letter back. We can read it together."

Ben thinks that is a good idea. He likes grandma. He likes letters. He says, "Yes, Sara, let's mail these cards to grandma. That will be fun."

Sara and Ben stop playing the game. They put the cards in an envelope. They write their names and grandma's address on it. They put a stamp on it. They go to the mailbox and mail the envelope. They hug each other. They are happy.

Sara and Ben are not selfish. They share their cards with grandma. They do not care about the score. They care about each other. They are good twins.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big hill with a lot of rocks and dirt. They want to climb the hill and see what is on the other side.

"Let's go, Ben!" Anna says. "Maybe we can find something cool!"

"OK, Anna!" Ben says. "But we need some gear first. We need a hat, a bottle of water, and a stick."

They run to their mom and dad, who are sitting on a bench. They ask them to provide them with some gear for their adventure.

"Sure, sweeties," mom says. "Here are your hats and your water bottles. And look, there is a stick over there. You can use it as a walking stick."

"Thank you, mom!" Anna and Ben say. They take their gear and run to the hill.

They start to climb the hill, using their stick to help them. They see some flowers, some bugs, and some birds. They have fun and talk to each other.

"Look, Anna!" Ben says. "I found something shiny!"

He picks up a metal coin from the ground. It has some strange marks on it.

"What is it, Ben?" Anna asks.

"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe it is ancient. Maybe it is from a long time ago, when people lived here."

"Wow, Ben!" Anna says. "That is amazing! Maybe it is worth a lot of money!"

They put the coin in their pocket and keep climbing. They are happy and curious. They want to see what else they can find on the hill.

Sara and Ben liked to play hide and seek in their big house. They had many rooms and places to hide, but their favorite was the wardrobe in their parents' bedroom. It was big and dark and had many clothes and shoes inside. Sometimes they would squeeze behind the coats and pretend they were in a secret land.

One day, they decided to play hide and seek again while their parents were out. Sara was the seeker and Ben was the hider. He ran to the wardrobe and opened the door. He saw a big suitcase on the floor that was not there before. He thought it would be a good hiding place, so he opened it and climbed inside. He closed the lid and waited for Sara to find him.

Sara looked for Ben in every room, but she could not find him. She started to feel worried and sad. She went to the wardrobe and opened the door. She saw the suitcase and thought it was strange. She heard a faint noise coming from inside. She was alert and curious. She moved the clothes and shoes and reached for the lid. She tried to open it, but it was locked. She heard Ben's voice saying, "Help, help, I'm stuck!"

Sara was scared and sorry. She did not know how to unlock the suitcase. She shouted for help, but no one heard her. She cried and hugged the suitcase, hoping that Ben would be okay. She did not know that the suitcase belonged to their parents, who were going on a long trip. She did not know that they would soon come back and take the suitcase to the airport. She did not know that Ben would never come out.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. Lily was bossy. She told Ben what to do and what to use. Ben did not like it.

"Ben, get me the flour from the cupboard!" Lily shouted. "We need it for the cake!"

Ben did not want to get the flour. He wanted to use the eggs and the milk. He liked to crack the eggs and pour the milk. He said no to Lily.

"No, Lily, I want to use the eggs and the milk!" Ben shouted back. "You are not the boss of me!"

Lily and Ben started to fight. They pushed and pulled and yelled. They made a big mess in the kitchen. Flour and eggs and milk were everywhere. They did not see Mom coming.

Mom was angry. She saw the mess and heard the noise. She did not like it.

"Stop it, Lily and Ben!" Mom shouted. "You are not chefs, you are naughty children! Go to your rooms and clean up!"

Lily and Ben were sad. They did not want to go to their rooms. They wanted to play and make yummy food. They said sorry to Mom and to each other.

"Sorry, Mom," Lily and Ben said. "Sorry, Ben," Lily said. "Sorry, Lily," Ben said.

Mom hugged them and said it was okay. She said they could play again later, but they had to be nice and share and listen. Lily and Ben nodded and smiled. They learned their lesson. They went to their rooms and cleaned up.

Tom and Mia were playing in the garden. They saw a big door with a lock. They wanted to see what was behind the door.

"Let's unlock the door!" Tom said. He found a key under a rock. He put the key in the lock and turned it. The door opened with a creak.

"Wow, look!" Mia said. Behind the door, there was a small room with many things. There were books, toys, clothes, and a big bowl.

"What is in the bowl?" Tom asked. He walked to the bowl and looked inside. The bowl was full of shiny stones. They were red, blue, green, and yellow. They sparkled in the light.

"They are so pretty!" Mia said. She picked up a stone and held it in her hand. It felt warm and smooth. She wanted to take it home.

"Wait, don't touch them!" Tom said. He saw a note on the wall. It said: "Do not touch the stones. They are mysterious. They can do magic. They can make you happy or sad. They can make you big or small. They can make you fly or fall. Be careful!"

Tom and Mia were scared. They dropped the stones and ran out of the room. They closed the door and locked it. They decided to never go back.

"Let's play something else!" Tom said.

"OK, let's play ball!" Mia said.

They ran to the garden and played ball. They forgot about the bowl and the stones. They were happy.

Lily liked to watch the sun rise every morning. She would wake up early and go to the window. She would see the sky change from dark to light. She would see the sun peek out from behind the hills. She would see the birds fly and sing. She felt a lot of wonder in her heart.

One morning, Lily wanted to see the sun rise closer. She put on her shoes and coat. She opened the door and went outside. She walked up the hill behind her house. She walked and walked until she was very tired. She was strong and brave.

When she reached the top of the hill, she saw the sun rise in front of her. It was big and bright and warm. It made the grass and the flowers and the trees glow. It made Lily smile and laugh. She felt happy and proud. She had seen the sun rise closer. She had done something new and amazing. She felt more wonder in her heart.

Sara and Ben like to play with copper. Copper is a shiny metal that they find in the park. They make rings and bracelets and necklaces with copper. They think copper is unique and pretty.

One day, they meet a new friend in the park. His name is Leo. Leo sees their copper jewelry and says, "Wow, what is that? Can I play with you?"

Sara and Ben smile and say, "Sure, this is copper. We find it in the park. We make jewelry with it. Do you want to try?"

Leo nods and says, "Yes, please. I have never seen copper before. It is so shiny and cool. How do you make jewelry with it?"

Sara and Ben show Leo how to bend and twist and shape the copper. They help him make a ring for his finger. Leo is very happy and says, "Thank you, Sara and Ben. You are very nice and creative. Can we be friends?"

Sara and Ben say, "Of course, Leo. We are happy to share our copper with you. You are very kind and curious. We can be friends and play together."

They hug and laugh and play with copper. They have a lot of fun and make more jewelry. They think copper is unique and so are they.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They liked to dig in the sand, splash in the water, and chase the birds. But they did not like to wash their hands and faces when they came home. They said it was boring and itchy.

One day, their mom told them they had a lovely surprise. She said they could go to the park and have a picnic with their friends. Anna and Ben were very happy and ran to get their hats and shoes. But mom stopped them and said, "Wait, you have to wash your hands and faces first. You are very dirty and you don't want to make your friends sick."

Anna and Ben did not want to wash. They said, "No, mom, we don't need to wash. We are not dirty and we are not sick. We have our own opinion and we think washing is silly."

Mom was not happy. She said, "I'm sorry, but you have to respect my opinion too. I am your mom and I know what is best for you. Washing is not silly, it is important and healthy. If you don't wash, you can't go to the park and have the picnic."

Anna and Ben did not like this. They wanted to go to the park and have the picnic. They looked at each other and decided to listen to mom. They said, "Okay, mom, we will wash. We are sorry for being rude. We love you and we want to make you happy."

Mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "Thank you, Anna and Ben. I love you too and I want to make you happy. I'm glad you understand that washing is good for you and for others. Now you can go to the park and have the picnic. And I have another lovely surprise for you. I made your favorite cookies for dessert."

Anna and Ben were very happy and thanked mom. They washed their hands and faces and went to the park. They had a lot of fun with their friends and enjoyed the picnic. They also shared their cookies with their friends and said they were delicious. They learned that washing was not so bad after all and that listening to mom was a good thing. They also learned that having an opinion was okay, but respecting other people's opinions was also important. They had a lovely day and went to bed with a smile.

Lily and Ben went to the museum with Mom and Dad. They saw many things in the museum. They saw big animals that looked like rocks. They saw small animals that had wings and colors. They saw old things that people made a long time ago.

Lily liked the museum, but Ben was bored. He wanted to play and run. He saw a big red button on the wall. It said "Do not push". Ben did not know what that meant. He thought it was a game. He pushed the button.

Suddenly, a loud noise came from the ceiling. Water started to spray everywhere. The people in the museum got wet and scared. They ran to the door. Lily, Mom and Dad also got wet. They looked for Ben.

Ben was hiding behind a big rock animal. He was sorry he pushed the button. He did not know it would make water come out. He was afraid Mom and Dad would be angry.

Mom and Dad found Ben. They were not angry, but they were not happy either. They told Ben he should not push buttons that say "Do not push". They said it was dangerous and rude. They said he should listen and learn in the museum, not play and run.

Ben said he was sorry. He said he would not push buttons again. He said he would try to like the museum. Lily gave him a hug. She said she still liked him. Mom and Dad gave him a hug too. They said they still loved him. They said they would go home and change their clothes. They said they would come back to the museum another day.

Lily liked to feel her thumb in her mouth. It made her calm and happy. She did not like to share her toys or her books. She kept them organized in her room. She did not want anyone to touch them or mess them up.

One day, her cousin Max came to visit. He wanted to play with Lily. He saw her toys and books and ran to them. He picked up a doll and a car and a book. He threw them on the floor. He laughed and said, "Let's play!"

Lily was angry. She ran to Max and pushed him. She yelled, "No! Those are mine! Go away!" She grabbed her toys and books and put them back in their places. She did not care that Max was crying. She did not care that he was hurt. She only cared about her things.

Max's mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Max on the floor with a bruise on his arm. She saw Lily with her thumb in her mouth and her toys and books organized. She was sad and angry. She said to Lily, "You are a bad girl. You hurt your cousin. You do not know how to share or be kind. You are selfish and mean. You have to say sorry to Max and give him a hug. And you have to let him play with your toys and books. Or you will have no friends and no fun."

Lily did not want to say sorry or hug Max. She did not want to let him play with her things. She shook her head and said, "No! I don't care. I like my thumb and my things. I don't need friends or fun."

Max's mom took Max and left. She said, "We will not come back until you learn how to be nice. Goodbye, Lily."

Lily was alone in her room. She felt her thumb in her mouth. She looked at her toys and books. They were organized. But they were not fun. They did not talk to her or hug her or laugh with her. They were just things. She felt sad and lonely. She wished she had a friend. She wished she had been nice to Max. She wished she had shared and played. But it was too late. She had made a bad choice. And she had to live with it.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Being kind is better than being organized. Friends are more important than things.

One day, a lion was very bored. He had nothing to do in his big cage. He looked at the other animals, but they were all dull. The monkeys were sleeping, the zebras were eating, and the elephants were spraying water. The lion wanted to have some fun.

He decided to roar very loud and scare the other animals. He opened his mouth and let out a big roar. RRRROOOOAAAARRR! The monkeys woke up and jumped. The zebras ran away. The elephants stopped spraying water and looked around. The lion laughed. He thought he was very clever.

But soon, the other animals got angry. They did not like the lion's roar. They wanted to be left alone. They started to make noises back at the lion. The monkeys screeched. The zebras neighed. The elephants trumpeted. The lion did not laugh anymore. He felt very annoyed.

He tried to roar louder, but the other animals did not stop. They made more and more noises. The lion could not hear himself roar. He felt very sad. He wished he had not roared at the other animals. He wished he had been nice to them.

He decided to say sorry to the other animals. He stopped roaring and walked to them. He looked at them with his big eyes and said, "I am sorry. I was bored. I did not mean to scare you. Can we be friends?" The other animals looked at the lion. They saw that he was sorry. They nodded and smiled. They said, "It's okay. We forgive you. We can be friends." The lion felt very happy. He had learned his lesson. He did not roar anymore. He played with the other animals. They had fun together. The lion was not bored anymore. He was glad.

Lily and Ben are playing with their blocks. They like to build towers and houses and cars. They also like to count their blocks and learn new numbers.

"Look, Lily, I have ten blocks in my tower!" Ben says, pointing to his tower. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!"

"Wow, Ben, that's a big number!" Lily says. "Can you show me how to make ten?"

"Sure, Lily, it's easy. You just need to add more blocks. Here, take some of mine." Ben gives Lily some of his blocks and helps her stack them on top of each other.

"Thank you, Ben. Now I have ten blocks too!" Lily says, pointing to her tower. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!"

They smile and clap their hands. They are proud of their towers and their numbers. They decide to make more towers and learn more numbers.

They play until their mom calls them for lunch. They put their blocks away and run to the kitchen. They are hungry and happy. They sit on their comfortable chairs and eat their sandwiches and fruits. They tell their mom about their towers and their numbers. Their mom listens and praises them. She is proud of them too.

Tom and Lily were twins who lived in a big house with their wealthy parents. They had many toys and books and clothes, but they were not happy. They always wanted more and more, and they never shared or said thank you.

One day, their parents had to go away for work, and they left Tom and Lily with their nanny, Mrs. Lee. Mrs. Lee was kind and patient, but she had rules. She told Tom and Lily to eat their breakfast, brush their teeth, and play nicely. But Tom and Lily did not listen. They threw their food on the floor, hid their toothbrushes, and fought over their toys.

Mrs. Lee was very sad and tired. She decided to rest on the couch for a while. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. Tom and Lily saw this and thought it was funny. They decided to play a prank on Mrs. Lee. They went to the kitchen and opened the freezer. They took out a big ice cream cake and carried it to the living room. They put the cake on Mrs. Lee's face and laughed.

But the cake was very cold and wet. It melted on Mrs. Lee's face and clothes and couch. It made a big mess. Mrs. Lee woke up and felt the cake. She was very angry and shocked. She screamed and cried. Tom and Lily were scared. They realized they had done a bad thing. They ran to their room and hid under their bed.

Mrs. Lee called their parents and told them what happened. Their parents were very disappointed and sorry. They came back home and scolded Tom and Lily. They made them clean up the mess and apologize to Mrs. Lee. They also took away their toys and books and clothes for a week. They told them to learn to be grateful and respectful and kind.

Tom and Lily felt very sorry and ashamed. They hugged Mrs. Lee and said they were sorry. They hugged their parents and said they loved them. They learned their lesson and promised to be better. They realized that being wealthy was not enough. They needed to be happy and good.

Sara and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a carrot nose. They were very happy.

But then, a big boy came. He was mean and rude. He said, "This is my snowman. Go away!" He pushed Sara and Ben and made them fall.

Sara and Ben were sad and scared. They did not want to fight. They said, "Please, don't be mean. We can share the snowman. It is big enough for all of us."

But the big boy did not listen. He said, "No, it is mine. I will make it bigger and better." He took some powder from his pocket and threw it on the snowman. He said, "This is magic powder. It will make the snowman grow and obey me."

But the powder was not magic. It was pepper. The snowman sneezed and sneezed. The hat and the carrot nose flew away. The snowman fell apart. The big boy was covered in snow and pepper. He cried and ran away.

Sara and Ben felt sorry for the big boy. They said, "He was not fit to play with us. He was selfish and rude. He did not know how to share and be kind."

They decided to make a new snowman. They used the hat and the carrot nose that they found. They also found a scarf and some buttons. They made the snowman smile. They said, "This is our snowman. He is happy and friendly. He likes to share and be kind."

They played with the snowman until it was time to go home. They said, "Goodbye, snowman. We will come back tomorrow. We hope you will not melt."

The moral of the story is: Sharing and kindness are better than selfishness and rudeness.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play in their room. They have a big mattress on the floor. They jump on the mattress and pretend to be mighty heroes.

One day, they hear a knock on the door. It is their mom. She has a surprise for them. She says, "Boys, I have something for you. Come and see."

Tom and Sam follow their mom to the living room. They see a big box. Their mom says, "This is your new bed. It is bigger and softer than the mattress. You can sleep on it and have sweet dreams."

Tom and Sam are very happy. They hug their mom and say, "Thank you, mom. We love you. Can we try the new bed?"

Their mom says, "Of course. But first, you have to help me move the mattress. It is very heavy. We need to put it in the garage."

Tom and Sam nod. They are strong boys. They help their mom lift the mattress. They carry it to the garage. They feel proud. They gain muscles and confidence.

They go back to the living room. They see their new bed. It is shiny and cozy. They climb on it and snuggle. They feel warm and safe. They say, "This is the best bed ever. We are lucky boys. We have a good mom and a good bed."

Their mom smiles. She says, "You are welcome, boys. I am glad you like it. Now, it is time for a nap. Sleep well, my mighty heroes."

Tom and Sam close their eyes. They fall asleep. They have sweet dreams.

Ben is a cheerful dog. He likes to run and play with his friends. He has a long tail that wags when he is happy. He likes to chase balls and sticks and birds.

One day, Ben sees a new dog in the park. The new dog is big and black and has a short tail. He does not look friendly. He barks loudly at Ben and his friends. He tries to take their balls and sticks and birds.

Ben is scared of the new dog. He does not want to play with him. He runs away and hides behind a tree. He frowns and tucks his tail between his legs. He is not cheerful anymore.

Then, he hears a whistle. It is his owner, Sam. Sam is looking for Ben. He loves Ben and wants to play with him. He sees Ben behind the tree and calls his name.

Ben hears Sam and runs to him. He is happy to see Sam. He wags his tail and licks Sam's face. He forgets about the new dog. He is cheerful again.

Sam throws a ball for Ben. Ben chases the ball and brings it back to Sam. He plays with Sam and his friends. He does not frown anymore. He has fun. He is a cheerful dog.

Lily liked to soar in the sky. She had a big red kite that her dad gave her. She would run and run and let the kite fly high. She felt happy and free.

One day, she went to the park with her dad and her kite. She saw a boy with a blue kite. He was also running and flying his kite. Lily wanted to play with him. She ran to him and said, "Hi, I like your kite. It is interesting. Can we be friends?"

The boy looked at Lily and her kite. He did not smile. He said, "No, I don't want to be friends. Your kite is boring. It is only red. My kite is better. It has stars and stripes. Go away."

Lily felt sad and angry. She did not like the boy. She said, "No, your kite is not better. My kite is faster and stronger. I will show you." She ran and pulled her kite hard. She wanted to make it soar higher than the boy's kite.

But she pulled too hard. Her kite broke. The string snapped and the kite fell to the ground. Lily cried. She lost her kite. She looked at the boy. He laughed. He said, "Ha ha, I told you. Your kite is boring and weak. My kite is the best. Bye bye, loser." He ran away with his kite.

Lily's dad came to her. He saw her kite on the ground. He saw her tears. He hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Your kite is broken. Don't worry, we can get a new one. Come on, let's go home." He picked up her kite and put it in his belt. He took her hand and walked to the car. Lily felt sad and sore. She did not want to soar anymore.

Sara and Tom like to jog with their dad. They put on their shoes and hats and go outside. Dad says, "Let's jog to the park and play on the swings."

They jog on the sidewalk and see many things. They see cars and dogs and flowers and birds. Sara and Tom point and say, "Look, dad, look!" Dad smiles and says, "Yes, I see, they are very nice."

They get to the park and see many kids. Some kids are on the swings, some are on the slide, some are on the seesaw. Sara and Tom want to play too. They say, "Dad, can we play on the swings?" Dad says, "Sure, but you have to wait your turn. There are other kids on the swings now."

Sara and Tom wait and watch the other kids. They see a girl with a pink dress and a boy with a blue shirt. They are swinging very high and laughing. Sara and Tom think they look fun. They say, "Hi, can we swing with you?" The girl and the boy say, "Hi, yes, you can. We are almost done. Do you want to push us?"

Sara and Tom say, "Yes, we do." They push the girl and the boy and make them go higher and higher. The girl and the boy say, "Wow, you are very good at pushing. Thank you!" Sara and Tom say, "You are welcome!"

Then the girl and the boy stop swinging and get off. They say, "Now it's your turn. We will push you." Sara and Tom say, "Thank you!" They get on the swings and the girl and the boy push them. Sara and Tom feel the wind in their hair and the sun on their face. They swing very high and laugh. They say, "This is fun! We like swinging!"

Dad watches them and smiles. He thinks, "They are very original. They make new friends easily." He is proud of Sara and Tom. He says, "I'm glad you are having fun. But don't forget, we have to jog back home soon." Sara and Tom say, "Okay, dad, we won't forget. But can we swing a little more?" Dad says, "Okay, a little more. But then we have to go." Sara and Tom say, "Okay, dad, we love you." Dad says, "I love you too."

Anna and her mom are going on a big plane to see grandma. Anna is very happy. She has a new backpack with a lot of colorful stickers. Mom has a big bag with clothes and books.

"Anna, do you have your passport?" mom asks. A passport is a small book with Anna's name and picture. It tells the people at the airport who she is and where she is going.

"Yes, mom, I have it right here," Anna says. She holds her passport in her hand. She likes to look at it. It has a blue cover and a shiny sticker.

"Good girl. Now, let's go to the gate. We have to show our passports to the lady there. She will give us tickets for the plane," mom says. She holds Anna's hand and they walk to the gate.

"Hello, can I see your passports, please?" the lady at the gate says. She has a red uniform and a big smile.

"Here you go," mom says. She gives the lady her passport and Anna's passport.

"Thank you. You are going to grandma's country. How exciting! Here are your tickets. Have a nice flight," the lady says. She gives mom and Anna two colorful tickets with numbers and letters.

"Thank you. Come on, Anna, let's go to the plane. It's time to fly," mom says.

"Yay! I can't wait to see grandma. And the plane. And the clouds. And the birds. And the..." Anna says. She holds her passport and her ticket in her backpack. She is very happy. She and mom go to the plane. They are ready for their adventure.

Lily and Ben were playing with blocks. They liked to build towers and houses and cars. But they did not like to share. Lily wanted all the blue blocks and Ben wanted all the red blocks. They started to fight and pull the blocks from each other.

"Give me that block!" Lily shouted.

"No, it's mine!" Ben yelled.

They were very grumpy and loud. Mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the mess of blocks and the angry faces of Lily and Ben.

"What are you doing?" Mom asked. "Why are you fighting?"

"Because she took my block!" Ben said.

"Because he took my block!" Lily said.

Mom shook her head. "That's not nice. You have to share and be kind. You have to attach the blocks together, not apart. Do you know what attach means?"

Lily and Ben looked at Mom. They did not know what attach meant.

"It means to put things together, to make them stick. Like this." Mom took two blocks and showed them how to attach them. "See? Now they are one. And you can attach more blocks and make something bigger and better. Like a bridge or a train or a castle. But if you pull them apart, you break them and make them smaller and worse. Like a pile of rubbish. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They understood. They felt sorry for being grumpy and mean. They said sorry to each other and to Mom. They decided to attach the blocks together and share them. They made a big rainbow tower and a happy house and a fast car. They had fun and laughed and hugged. Mom smiled and praised them.

"Good job, Lily and Ben. You learned how to attach and how to be friends. That's very important. I'm proud of you. Now, do you want a snack?"

Lily and Ben said yes and ran to the kitchen. They were hungry and thirsty. They thanked Mom for the snack and for the lesson. They learned that today was a good day to attach and to be happy.

Tim and Kim like to race. They race with their bikes, their feet, and their cars. They race in the park, in the street, and in the yard. They race every day, because racing is fun.

One day, they see a big, white dog in the park. The dog is wild. It has no collar, no leash, and no owner. It runs fast and barks loud. It scares the other dogs and the people. Tim and Kim want to race with the dog.

They get on their bikes and follow the dog. The dog sees them and runs faster. Tim and Kim pedal hard and try to catch up. They race past the trees, the swings, and the pond. They race with the wild, white dog.

But the dog is too fast and too smart. It turns and runs into the woods. Tim and Kim cannot follow. They stop and look at each other. They are tired and out of breath. They smile and laugh. They had a good race with the wild, white dog. They go back to the park and race some more.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play with their toys and watch TV. But they do not like to eat their meal. Mom always makes them eat vegetables and soup. They think it is yucky and boring.

One day, Mom is busy in the kitchen. She tells Lily and Tom to eat their meal and then watch TV. Lily and Tom do not listen. They sneak to the living room and turn on the TV. They watch a funny show with animals and laugh.

Mom hears them and comes to the living room. She is angry. She turns off the TV and says, "Lily and Tom, you are very naughty. You did not eat your meal. You only watch TV. That is stupid. TV is not good for you. You need to eat your meal to grow big and strong. Now go back to the table and finish your meal. No more TV for you today."

Lily and Tom are sad and scared. They do not want to make Mom angry. They do not want to miss their show. They do not want to eat their meal. They cry and say, "But Mom, we do not like our meal. It is yucky and boring. We like TV. It is funny and fun. Please let us watch TV. Please do not be mad at us."

Mom shakes her head and says, "No, Lily and Tom. You have to eat your meal first. Then you can watch TV later. It is not stupid to eat your meal. It is smart. It makes you healthy and happy. TV is not everything. You can watch it another time. Now stop crying and go back to the table. I will help you eat your meal. And then I will hug you and tell you I love you."

Lily and Tom do not want to argue with Mom. They know she loves them and wants them to be good. They wipe their tears and go back to the table. They eat their meal with Mom's help. They do not like it, but they try to be brave. They hope Mom will let them watch TV tomorrow. They hope Mom will hug them and tell them she loves them. They love Mom too.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their ball. One day, they see a big zigzag on the grass. It is a snake. The snake is sleeping in the sun.

"Look, a snake!" Ben says. He wants to touch it. He is not careful.

"No, Ben, don't!" Anna says. She is scared. She knows snakes can bite. She tries to stop him.

But Ben does not listen. He runs to the snake. He disturbs it. The snake wakes up. It is angry. It hisses and coils. It shows its teeth.

"Help, help!" Ben cries. He is sorry. He runs back to Anna. Anna hugs him. She is glad he is safe.

The snake slithers away. It wants to be alone.

Anna and Ben learn a lesson. They should not disturb animals. They should be careful and respectful. They should listen to each other. They should play with their ball instead.

Sam likes to play with his red truck. He drives it on the floor and makes loud noises. He pretends he is a big truck driver. He has a lot of fun.

One day, he sees a big hole in the yard. He thinks it is a good place to park his truck. He runs to the hole with his truck. He puts his truck in the hole and smiles. He thinks his truck is safe and happy.

But then, he hears a loud sound. It is the water hose. His mom is watering the flowers. She does not see the hole or the truck. She sprays water on the hole. The hole starts to fill with water. Sam sees the water and gets scared. He runs to the hole and tries to get his truck. But the water is too deep and too fast. He cannot reach his truck. He feels his foot get wet. He cries.

His mom hears him cry and turns off the hose. She sees the hole and the truck. She sees Sam's wet foot and sad face. She feels sorry for Sam. She says, "Oh, Sam, I'm sorry. I did not know your truck was there. It was an accident. Don't cry. We can get your truck out. It will be okay."

She goes to the shed and gets a big shovel. She digs the hole and makes the water go away. She finds the truck and gives it to Sam. She says, "Here is your truck, Sam. It is wet, but it is not broken. You can dry it and play with it again. It is a good truck. You are a good truck driver."

Sam takes his truck and hugs it. He says, "Thank you, mom. You are a good mom. You saved my truck. I love you." He smiles.

He learns a lesson. He learns that holes can fill with water. He learns that he should not park his truck in holes. He learns that his mom is serious about watering the flowers. He learns that his mom loves him and helps him. He is happy.

Tom and Lily like to play with their toys. They have many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, animals, and more. They make a lot of mess in their room. Their mom tells them to organize their toys. She says, "Put your toys in the right boxes. Make your room neat and tidy. Then you can go to the museum with me."

Tom and Lily do not listen to their mom. They think organizing is hard and boring. They want to go to the museum now. They say, "Mom, we are ready. Let's go to the museum. We want to see the dinosaurs and the paintings and the stars."

Their mom is not happy. She says, "No, you are not ready. Your room is still a mess. You have to organize your toys first. It is easy if you do it together. If you do not organize your toys, you cannot go to the museum."

Tom and Lily are angry. They do not want to organize their toys. They do not want to do it together. They start to fight. They throw their toys at each other. They break their toys. They make more mess. They make a lot of noise.

Their mom hears the noise. She comes to their room. She sees the broken toys and the mess. She is very angry. She says, "That's it. You are not going to the museum. You are going to stay in your room and clean up. You are also going to say sorry to each other and to me. You have been very naughty and selfish."

Tom and Lily are sad. They cry. They wish they had listened to their mom. They wish they had organized their toys. They wish they had gone to the museum. They learn a lesson. They learn that organizing is easy and fun if they do it together. They learn that they have to respect their mom and their toys. They learn that they have to be good and kind to each other.

Lily loved to cook with her mom. They made healthy food like soup, salad and fruit. Lily liked to taste everything and help mom stir and chop. Mom taught Lily how to use the knife carefully and wash her hands.

One day, Lily found mom's diary on the table. She was curious and opened it. She saw mom's writing and drawings. She wanted to read them, but the words were too hard. She tried to copy some of the words on a paper, but she made a mess.

Mom came back and saw Lily with her diary and the paper. She was angry and sad. She said, "Lily, this is my diary. It is private. You should not touch it or write on it. You hurt my feelings."

Lily felt sorry and scared. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I just wanted to read your diary. I like your writing and drawings. I want to be like you."

Mom hugged Lily and said, "I love you, Lily. I know you want to learn, but you have to respect other people's things. If you want to read my diary, you can ask me. I can share some of it with you. And if you want to write and draw, you can use your own notebook. I can help you with the words."

Lily nodded and said, "Thank you, mom. I'm sorry again. Can we cook together again?"

Mom smiled and said, "Of course, we can. Cooking is fun and healthy. And it is something we can share."

The moral value of the story is: respect other people's privacy and belongings, and ask for permission before using them.

Anna and Ben like to help their mom cook. They have their own equipment: a small pot, a spoon, a bowl and a apron. Mom lets them cook some soup with carrots, potatoes and water.

"Can I put some salt in the soup?" Ben asks mom.

"Yes, but only a little bit. Salt makes food tasty, but too much salt makes food bitter," mom says.

Anna wants to put some salt too. She takes the salt shaker and shakes it over the pot. But she shakes it too hard and a lot of salt falls into the soup.

"Oh no, Anna, you put too much salt!" Ben says.

Anna feels sorry. She did not mean to put too much salt. She hopes the soup is still good.

Mom tastes the soup. She makes a face. The soup is very bitter.

"I'm sorry, mom. I put too much salt," Anna says.

"It's okay, Anna. It was an accident. We can fix the soup. We can add some more water and some milk. That will make the soup less bitter," mom says.

She adds some water and some milk to the pot and stirs the soup. She tastes it again. The soup is better now. It is not bitter anymore.

"Good job, mom. The soup is yummy now," Ben says.

Anna smiles. She is happy that the soup is yummy. She and Ben help mom serve the soup in bowls. They eat the soup with bread and butter. They enjoy their lunch. They like to cook with mom.

Tom and Sue were having lunch with Mom. Mom gave them some salad and cheese. Tom liked cheese, but Sue did not. She made a face when she tasted it.

"Yuck, this cheese is bitter!" Sue said. "I don't want it."

Mom smiled and said, "You don't have to eat it, Sue. But you should try new things sometimes. You might like them."

Sue shook her head and pushed the cheese away. She picked up her fork and stabbed a tomato. She liked tomatoes. They were juicy and sweet.

Tom saw Sue's fork and wanted to play with it. He reached for it and said, "Give me your fork, Sue. I want to make a tower with it."

Sue did not want to share her fork. She said, "No, Tom. This is my fork. You have your own fork. Go away."

Tom did not listen. He grabbed Sue's fork and pulled it hard. Sue held on to it and pulled it back. They both pulled and pulled until the fork snapped in half.

"Ow!" Tom cried. He dropped the fork and held his hand. He had cut his finger on the sharp edge of the fork. It hurt and it bled.

Mom heard Tom's cry and came to see what happened. She saw the broken fork and Tom's finger. She said, "Oh, no! What did you do, Tom? You should not play with forks. They are sharp and dangerous. They are for eating, not for playing."

She took Tom to the sink and washed his finger. She put a band-aid on it and gave him a hug. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I hope you feel better soon. Next time, be careful with forks and ask nicely if you want to share something."

Tom nodded and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, Sue. I won't play with forks again. Can I have some cheese, please?"

Sue looked at Tom and said, "You can have some of my cheese, Tom. But only if you say thank you."

Tom said, "Thank you, Sue. You are a good sister."

Sue smiled and said, "You are welcome, Tom. You are a good brother."

They both ate their cheese and salad and were happy. Mom was happy, too. She threw away the broken fork and got a new one for Sue. She said, "That's a good story, kids. Now, let's finish our lunch and have some cake for dessert."

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they see a poster on the wall. The poster says: "Come to the fair! Win a prize! Have fun!"

Anna and Ben want to go to the fair. They ask their moms to take them. Their moms say yes. They are happy.

At the fair, they see many things. They see balloons, animals, games, and rides. They want to try everything. They play a game where they throw balls at cans. If they knock down all the cans, they win a prize.

Anna throws a ball. She misses. She tries again. She misses again. She is sad.

Ben throws a ball. He hits a can. He throws another ball. He hits another can. He throws the last ball. He knocks down all the cans. He wins a prize. He is happy.

He looks at the prizes. He sees a teddy bear, a car, a doll, and a hat. He likes the teddy bear. It is brown and soft and cute. He picks the teddy bear.

He goes to Anna. He says: "Look, Anna, I won a prize. It is a teddy bear. Do you like it?"

Anna says: "Yes, Ben, I like it. It is very cute. You are very good at the game."

Ben says: "Thank you, Anna. You are very nice. Do you want the teddy bear? You can have it. It is for you."

Anna says: "Really, Ben? For me? Thank you, thank you, thank you! You are very kind. I love the teddy bear. It is the best prize ever."

They hug each other. They hug the teddy bear. They are happy. They go to see more things at the fair. They have fun.

Lily and Max were playing outside with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and catch it. The sky was blue and the sun was bright.

Suddenly, they heard a loud boom. They looked up and saw dark clouds and flashes of lightning. They were scared and ran to their house.

"Mama, mama, there is lightning!" Lily cried.

Mama came to the door and hugged them. "Don't worry, my loves, it's just a storm. It will pass soon. Come inside and we'll have some cookies and milk."

She took them to the kitchen and gave them a plate of cookies and two glasses of milk. She turned on the radio and played some calm music. She told them stories about the rain and the thunder and the lightning.

Lily and Max listened and ate their cookies. They felt better and less scared. They learned that lightning was a big spark of electricity in the sky. They learned that thunder was the sound of lightning. They learned that rain was water falling from the clouds.

They looked out the window and saw a rainbow. They smiled and hugged their mama. They thanked her for the cookies and the milk and the stories. They were happy and calm. The storm was over.

Tim and Lily were playing in the yard. They liked to jump in the big pile of leaves that dad made with the rake. The rake was long and had many teeth. It could make the leaves move and make a crunchy sound.

But one day, when they were playing, they heard a loud roar. It came from behind the pile of leaves. Tim and Lily were scared. They thought it was a big, mean animal that wanted to eat them. They ran to the house and told mom.

Mom said, "Don't worry, it's not a big, mean animal. It's just the neighbor's dog. He likes to play in the leaves too. He's very friendly and fluffy. Do you want to meet him?"

Tim and Lily nodded. They wanted to be brave and make a new friend. Mom took them to the pile of leaves and called the dog. The dog came out, wagging his tail and licking his nose. He was brown and white and had a red collar.

"His name is Spot," mom said. "He likes to play fetch and get belly rubs. Do you want to play with him?"

Tim and Lily smiled. They liked Spot. They took the rake and threw a stick for him. Spot ran after the stick and brought it back. He dropped it at their feet and rolled on his back. Tim and Lily gave him belly rubs and laughed. They were not scared anymore. They had found a new friend.

Lily liked to play with clay. She could make many things with clay. She could make balls, snakes, stars, and flowers. She liked to show her clay things to her mom and dad. They always said, "Good job, Lily!"

One day, Lily wanted to make a clay house. She had a big piece of clay. She rolled it and flattened it and cut it. She made four walls and a roof. She put them together with more clay. She made a door and a window. She was very happy with her clay house.

She wanted to show her clay house to her mom and dad. She picked it up carefully and walked to the living room. But on the way, she tripped on a toy. She fell down and dropped her clay house. It broke into many pieces. Lily was very upset. She cried and cried.

Her mom and dad heard her cry. They came to see what happened. They saw the broken clay house and the toy. They hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, Lily. We're sorry your clay house broke. We know you worked hard on it. But you can make another one. You can succeed again. We love you, Lily."

Lily stopped crying. She looked at her mom and dad. She felt better. She said, "Thank you, mom and dad. I love you, too. I will make another clay house. And I will be careful with the toy." She smiled and hugged them back. She picked up the clay pieces and went back to her room. She was ready to try again.

Lily liked to stretch her lip with her fingers. She thought it was funny to make faces in the mirror. She also liked to stretch her lip when she was bored or angry. She did not know that stretching her lip too much could hurt it.

One day, Lily went to the store with her mom. She saw a cheap toy that she wanted. It was a doll with long hair and a pink dress. She asked her mom to buy it for her, but her mom said no. Lily was very angry. She started to cry and scream. She also stretched her lip with her fingers.

"Stop that, Lily," her mom said. "You will hurt your lip if you stretch it too much. And you don't need that cheap toy. It will break soon."

Lily did not listen to her mom. She kept crying and stretching her lip. She wanted the toy so badly. She did not care about her lip.

But then, something bad happened. Lily stretched her lip so much that it tore. She felt a sharp pain and saw blood on her fingers. She was scared and shocked. She stopped crying and looked at her mom.

"Mommy, mommy, it hurts!" she said. "My lip is broken!"

Her mom hugged her and took her to the bathroom. She cleaned her lip and put a band-aid on it. She also gave her a kiss and said she was sorry.

"Lily, I'm sorry you hurt your lip," her mom said. "But you have to be careful with your body. You can't stretch your lip like that. It's not good for you."

Lily nodded and said she was sorry too. She learned her lesson. She did not stretch her lip anymore. She also did not want the cheap toy anymore. She realized that it was not worth it. She was happy with her mom and her band-aid.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many colorful leaves. Lily wanted to climb the tree and see the sky. Tom was scared of the tree. He said, "No, Lily, do not climb the tree. It is too high and you can fall."

But Lily did not listen to Tom. She said, "I want to climb the tree. It is fun and pretty. You are a baby and you are afraid." She ran to the tree and started to climb. She grabbed the branches and the leaves. She went higher and higher.

Tom watched Lily from the ground. He was worried. He said, "Lily, come down. It is not safe. You can hurt yourself." But Lily did not hear Tom. She was too busy climbing the tree. She was happy and proud. She said, "Look, Tom, I am on the top of the tree. I can see everything. I am the best climber."

But then, something bad happened. Lily saw a shiny thing on a branch. She reached for it. It was a needle. Someone had left it on the tree. Lily did not know what a needle was. She thought it was a toy. She touched the needle with her hand. It was sharp and it poked her. It made her bleed and it hurt a lot.

Lily screamed and let go of the branch. She fell from the tree. She hit the ground hard. She was hurt and she cried. Tom ran to her and hugged her. He said, "Lily, I am sorry. You are hurt. I will get help." He called for a grown-up. A grown-up came and took Lily to the doctor. The doctor gave her a band-aid and a hug. He said, "Lily, you are brave. But you should not climb the tree. It is dangerous. You should listen to your friend. He cares about you."

Lily was sad and sorry. She said, "I am sorry, Tom. You were right. I should not have climbed the tree. I was silly and mean. You are a good friend. Can you forgive me?" Tom said, "I forgive you, Lily. You are my friend. But please, do not climb the tree again. It is not worth it." Lily said, "I promise, Tom. I will not climb the tree again. I will play with you on the ground. It is safer and more fun." They hugged and smiled. But Lily's hand still hurt and she had a scar. She learned a hard lesson. Climbing the tree was a bad idea.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to make up stories with their dolls and cars. Lily had a big box of photos that her mom gave her. She liked to look at them and see the faces of her family and friends.

"Look, Ben, this is a photo of me and you when we were babies," Lily said, holding up a picture. "We were so small and cute. Do you remember?"

Ben shook his head. He did not remember being a baby. He only remembered being a big boy who could run and jump and talk.

"Mom says we were very lively babies. We liked to laugh and play and make noise. We still do, right?" Lily asked.

Ben nodded. He liked to laugh and play and make noise with Lily. They were best friends.

"Who is this?" Ben asked, pointing to another photo. It showed a man with a big smile and a hat. He was holding Lily in his arms.

"That's my dad. He lives far away now. He works on a big boat. He sends me letters and stickers sometimes. I miss him a lot," Lily said, feeling sad.

Ben hugged Lily. He knew how it felt to miss someone. His dad also lived far away. He worked on a big plane. He also sent him letters and stickers sometimes.

"Maybe our dads will come back soon. Maybe they will play with us and take us to the park. That would be fun, right?" Ben said, trying to cheer Lily up.

Lily smiled. She hoped Ben was right. She loved her dad and wanted to see him again.

"Maybe they will. And maybe they will take a photo of us together. Then we can put it in the box and look at it when we miss them. That would remind us of them, right?" Lily said.

Ben agreed. He liked that idea. He liked photos. They reminded him of happy times. He and Lily decided to make a card for their dads. They used crayons and stickers and wrote "We love you" on it. They put the card in an envelope and asked their mom to mail it. They hoped their dads would like it. They hoped their dads would come back soon. They hoped they would be a happy family again.

Lily liked to touch things. She liked to touch soft things, like her teddy bear and her blanket. She liked to touch hard things, like her blocks and her spoon. She liked to touch warm things, like her mom and her soup. She liked to touch cold things, like her ice cream and her snowman.

But Lily did not like to touch sour things. Sour things made her face scrunch up and her tongue sting. She did not like lemons, or vinegar, or pickles. She did not like sour things at all.

One Sunday, Lily went to the park with her dad. She saw a big tree with yellow fruits. She wondered what they were. She asked her dad, and he said they were grapefruits. He said they were good for you, but they were a little sour. Lily wanted to try one. She asked her dad to pick one for her. He did, and he peeled it for her. He gave her a slice and said, "Be careful, it might be sour."

Lily took a bite. She felt a burst of juice in her mouth. She felt a sour taste on her tongue. She felt her face scrunch up and her tongue sting. She did not like it. She spit it out and said, "Yuck! Sour! No like!"

Her dad laughed and hugged her. He said, "It's okay, Lily. You don't have to like everything. Here, have some water. It will make your tongue feel better."

Lily drank some water. She felt her tongue feel better. She smiled and said, "Thank you, dad. Water good. Grapefruit bad."

Her dad smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I love you. Let's go play on the swings."

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, dad. I love you too. Swings fun."

They went to the swings and had a good time. Lily forgot about the sour grapefruit. She only remembered the sweet water and the warm hug. She was happy. It was a good Sunday.

Sam and Mia love to play at the beach. They like to make sand castles, find shells and splash in the water. One day, they see a big surf board near the shore. It is red and shiny and has a rope on it.

"Wow, look at that!" Sam says. "Can we try it?"

"I don't know," Mia says. "It looks hard to use. And maybe it belongs to someone."

"Let's ask Mom," Sam says. They run to their mom, who is sitting on a towel with a book. "Mom, can we use that surf board? Please?"

Mom looks at the surf board and smiles. "Sure, you can use it. But be careful, okay? And stay close to me. The surf board is for the water, not for the sand."

"Yay, thank you, Mom!" Sam and Mia say. They grab the rope and drag the surf board to the water. They take turns to sit on it and paddle with their hands. They feel the waves lift them up and down. They laugh and shout with joy.

"Look, Mom, I'm surfing!" Sam says.

"Me too, me too!" Mia says.

They have so much fun that they don't notice a hidden rock under the water. When a big wave comes, the surf board hits the rock and flips over. Sam and Mia fall into the water. They are scared and wet. They cry for help.

"Mom, Mom, help us!" they scream.

Mom hears them and runs to the water. She grabs the rope and pulls the surf board back. She helps Sam and Mia to get on it. She hugs them and calms them down.

"Are you okay, my sweeties?" she asks.

"Yes, Mom, we're okay," Sam and Mia say. "But we're sorry. We broke the surf board."

Mom looks at the surf board and sees a crack on it. She sighs and says, "Don't worry, we can fix it. Or we can buy a new one. The important thing is that you are safe and happy. But next time, be more careful, okay? And watch out for hidden rocks."

"Okay, Mom, we will," Sam and Mia say. They hug Mom and say, "We love you, Mom."

"I love you too, my darlings," Mom says. She smiles and says, "Now, let's go and have some ice cream. How does that sound?"

"Yummy, yummy, ice cream!" Sam and Mia say. They release the rope and leave the surf board on the shore. They follow Mom to the ice cream truck. They forget about the surf board and the hidden rock. They only think about the ice cream and the fun they had. They are happy.

Lily and Ben are best friends. They like to play pretend. Sometimes they pretend to be animals, or pirates, or superheroes. Today they pretend to be doctors.

Lily has a white coat and a stethoscope. Ben has a bandage and a hat. They find a teddy bear and put it on the couch. "This is our patient," Lily says. "He is sick. We have to make him better."

Ben nods. He looks at the teddy bear with his stethoscope. "He has a fever," he says. "And a sore throat. And a cough." He wraps the bandage around the teddy bear's neck. "There, that will help."

Lily smiles. She takes her finger and pretends it is a needle. "He also needs a shot," she says. "It will make him strong and healthy." She gently pokes the teddy bear with her finger. "Don't worry, it won't hurt."

The teddy bear does not say anything. He just looks at Lily and Ben with his big eyes. He thinks they are very kind. He feels better already. He gives them a hug and a kiss. "Thank you, doctors," he says. "You are the best."

Lily and Ben hug him back. They are happy. They like to play pretend. They like to help their friends. They are kind doctors.

Tom and Lily were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and look at the water. Sometimes they saw fish or birds or boats. But today they saw something big and gray and spouty. It was a whale!

"Wow, look at that whale!" Tom said. "It is so big and strong and loud!"

"I want to see it closer!" Lily said. "Maybe it will talk to us or play with us!"

Mom and dad shook their heads. "No, Lily, you can't go near the whale. It is too far and too deep and too dangerous. The whale might not like it if you bother it. It might get angry or scared or hurt you."

"But why?" Lily asked. "The whale looks nice and friendly. It is just swimming and splashing and having fun. Maybe it is lonely and wants some friends."

Tom decided to agree with Lily. He thought mom and dad were ignorant. They did not know anything about whales. He wanted to learn more about them and make them happy. He said to Lily, "Let's go find the whale. We can sneak away when mom and dad are not looking. We can swim to it and say hello and give it a hug."

Lily nodded. She thought Tom was brave and smart. She wanted to go with him and see the whale. She said to Tom, "OK, let's go. But we have to be quick and quiet. We don't want mom and dad to stop us."

They waited until mom and dad were busy with their books and towels. Then they ran to the water and jumped in. They swam as fast as they could, following the whale's spout. They did not see the big waves or the sharp rocks or the other animals. They only saw the whale.

They got closer and closer to the whale. They saw its eyes and mouth and fins and tail. They saw its skin and teeth and blowhole. They thought it was beautiful and amazing. They smiled and waved and shouted, "Hi, whale! We are Tom and Lily! We want to be your friends!"

The whale heard them and saw them. It did not smile or wave or shout back. It did not want to be their friends. It did not like them at all. It thought they were annoying and rude and stupid. It decided to teach them a lesson.

It opened its mouth and sucked them in. It swallowed them whole. It felt them squirm and scream in its belly. It felt satisfied and proud and happy.

It spouted a big jet of water and dived deeper into the sea. It left behind mom and dad, who were looking for Tom and Lily. They did not see the whale or hear their children. They only saw the water and felt the fear and the sadness.

Lila and Max were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw a new girl with a big doll. The doll had long hair, a pretty dress and shiny shoes. Lila and Max looked at the doll and felt envious.

"Wow, look at her doll!" Lila said. "It is so big and nice. I wish I had a doll like that."

"Me too," Max said. "Maybe we can ask her to play with us and share her doll."

They walked over to the new girl and said hello. The new girl smiled and said her name was Mia. She held her doll close to her waist.

"Hi, Mia. We are Lila and Max. Can we play with you and your doll?" Lila asked.

"Sure, you can play with me. But you can't touch my doll. She is mine and I love her very much. She is the best doll in the world," Mia said.

Lila and Max felt sad. They wanted to play with the doll, but Mia did not want to share. They thought Mia was not very nice. They looked at each other and had an idea.

"Okay, Mia. We will play with you. But we have a game for you. It is called 'seem'. Do you know how to play?" Max asked.

"No, I don't. How do you play?" Mia asked.

"It is easy. You just have to say what things seem like. For example, I can say 'the sky seems blue' or 'the grass seems green'. Do you understand?" Max explained.

"I think so. It sounds fun. Let's play," Mia said.

"Okay, you go first. What does your doll seem like?" Lila asked.

Mia looked at her doll and smiled. She said, "My doll seems like a princess. She has beautiful hair, a lovely dress and sparkly shoes. She is the most wonderful doll ever."

Lila and Max nodded. They waited for Mia to look away. Then they quickly grabbed the doll and ran away. They laughed and said, "Your doll seems like ours now. Bye, Mia!"

Mia was shocked and angry. She shouted and cried. She wanted her doll back. She did not like the game of 'seem'. She thought Lila and Max were very mean. She wished she had shared her doll with them.

Anna loved animals. She wanted to be a veterinarian when she grew up. She liked to read books about animals and watch them on TV. She also liked to play with her stuffed animals and pretend they were sick or hurt. She would use her toy stethoscope and bandages to make them feel better.

One day, Anna went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw a lot of animals there. She saw birds, squirrels, dogs, and cats. She wanted to pet them all, but her mom and dad told her to be careful and ask the owners first. Anna was impatient. She wanted to touch the animals and hear their hearts.

She saw a big dog with a red collar. He looked friendly and wagged his tail. Anna ran towards him, but he barked and growled. He did not like strangers. Anna was scared and cried. The dog's owner came and apologized. He said his dog was nervous and needed to see a veterinarian. He said the veterinarian would help his dog feel calm and happy.

Anna felt sorry for the dog. She wondered what a veterinarian was. She asked her mom and dad. They explained that a veterinarian was a doctor for animals. They said a veterinarian could check the animals' health and give them medicine or surgery if they needed it. They said a veterinarian could also teach the owners how to take care of their animals and prevent them from getting sick or hurt.

Anna was amazed. She wanted to learn more about veterinarians. She decided to be more patient and respectful with the animals. She thought that maybe one day, she could be a veterinarian too. She smiled and hugged her stuffed animals. She said she would take them to the veterinarian if they ever felt bad. She said she loved animals and wanted to help them.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing on the swings and slide on the slide. But today, one of the swings was broken. The seat had a big hole in it and the chain was loose.

"Oh no, we can't swing on this one," said Ben. "It's not safe."

"Maybe we can repair it," said Lily. "We can find some things to fix it."

They looked around the park and found some sticks, some leaves, and some string. They tried to patch the hole with the leaves and tie the chain with the string. They worked hard and had fun.

"Look, we did it!" said Lily. "We repaired the swing!"

They ran to the swing and tried to sit on it. But as soon as they did, the leaves fell off and the string snapped. The swing was still broken.

"Oops, it didn't work," said Ben. "We need something stronger."

Just then, a man came to the park. He had a toolbox and a ladder. He was wearing a hat that said "Park Ranger".

"Hello, kids," he said. "I'm here to repair the swing. I have the right tools and materials. Do you want to help me?"

"Yes, please!" said Ben and Lily. "We tried to repair it, but we couldn't."

"That's very kind of you to try," said the man. "But sometimes you need a professional. Here, you can hold this wrench and this hammer. And you can hand me these nails and this board. Together, we can make the swing good as new."

Ben and Lily helped the man repair the swing. They learned how to use the tools and how to measure and cut the board. They were very careful and listened to the man's instructions.

"There, we're done," said the man. "Now the swing has a new seat and a strong chain. Do you want to try it?"

"Yes, thank you!" said Ben and Lily. "You're very kind to repair the swing for us and let us help you."

They climbed on the swing and swung high and low. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They laughed and smiled.

They were happy to play on the repaired swing.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was ready to go to the park with his mom. He put on his jacket and shoes, and they walked to the park together.

At the park, Tim saw a big tree. He wanted to climb it. But a girl named Sally was there too. She said, "I want to climb the tree first!" Tim and Sally both wanted to climb the tree at the same time. They did not know what to do.
